correctness.rationale: For the specified pair-creation Uθ and initially I/2 target with independent bath ancillas diag(1−p,p), the excited population exactly a_k=q−(1−2p)(1−t)^k/2. The partially transposed 2×2 odd-parity block has a negative eigenvalue precisely for 4t(1−t)r² x_k²>4p(1−p)[1−r²(1−x_k)²], x_k=(1−t)^k. The quadratic has one positive root X_*; integer strict crossing gives N_p(t)=max(0,ceil(log X_*/log(1−t))). The first-contact optimum t(1−t)≤1/4 yields p<(1−1/√2)/2. For t=ap, pN→max(0,log((1+a)/2))/a; uniform upper bound excludes a→0,∞ and unique maximizer a*=3.311070407 gives K*=1/(a*+1)=0.23196095. Physical independent two-qubit partial-transpose and reset trajectory checks agreed on sampled p,t,k, but proof covers all.
